Cite this lesson Video Summary for Producer Price Index The Producer Price Index (PPI) is a key economic indicator that tracks wholesale prices before products reach consumers. This video explains how economists use the PPI to predict inflation trends in the economy. The PPI compares the average costs of a standard basket of goods over time at the wholesale level, formerly known as the Wholesale Price Index. Published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the PPI is categorized into three types: Industry-based (like integrated circuits) Commodity-based (like computer monitors) Stage-of-processing-based (products not in final form) The video demonstrates how to calculate PPI using a baseline year set at 100, typically December 1982. By tracking these wholesale price changes, economists can anticipate consumer price increases and inflation rates, making the producer price index a valuable predictive economic tool.
